run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T12:27:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing on HTTP 504 responses returned by the frontend-proxy's ingress (server) spans at a fixed ~15.0s duration, which began around 12:27-12:30Z. Those 504s coincide with checkout's order flow blocking for ~30s: checkout's own HTTP client spans to the email service (Post http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation, i.e. ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080) fail with 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' after 30.00s, and its parent oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans last 30.09-30.40s. checkout's pod logs repeat the same dial-timeout error from 12:27:53Z onward. The email service itself has two Running/Ready pods with valid endpoints, no restarts, stable ~51MB memory, and serves the connections that do get through with HTTP 200 in 3.6-64ms, so the failure is at TCP connection establishment to the email service ClusterIP, not in email's request handling, not a pod crash/OOM, and not a frontend-proxy-local failure. The deepest confirmed cause is checkout's blocked email calls surfacing as frontend-proxy 504s; why new TCP connections to the email ClusterIP time out is not determinable from the available evidence (no packet/conntrack/CNI-policy or per-endpoint reachability data).

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error spans occur only on operation 'ingress'; its error rate rose from a baseline of 0.000-0.015 spans/s to 0.20-0.35 spans/s starting with the 12:30:32Z sample, while operation 'router frontend egress' had an error rate of 0 throughout 12:10:32-12:40:32Z.

Sampled frontend-proxy ingress error spans carry error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of about 15,000,000 microseconds (e.g. span 317f5eeff095f1f6, duration 15,001,496 us).
In the same sampled traces the load-generator's POST client span records the same 504 error, and the paired frontend POST server span ran 15,000,276 us while recording only http.status_code=200.

Among all services' ERROR-status span rates in 11:27:32-12:46:00Z, only frontend-proxy and checkout were clearly elevated; accounting, payment, frontend, ad, fraud-detection and recommendation all read approximately 0 (frontend exactly 0 across every sample).

checkout's error spans are all operation 'HTTP POST'; its error rate first became nonzero at the 12:30:32Z sample (0.0627/s) and peaked at 0.1868/s at 12:36:32Z, while its other operations (PlaceOrder, CartService/GetCart, CartService/EmptyCart, PaymentService/Charge, CurrencyService/Convert, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct) carried no ERROR status.

checkout's failing HTTP POST spans last 30.00s and carry otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; their visible parent spans are operation oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder lasting 30,085,339-30,396,865 us (e.g. span 3fc1cb1fa7fba96a -> 03299e4e83d07e3f, and 12fafd848ff9ae99 -> 8f36556b0a5a45b9).
100.67.49.77:8080 is the ClusterIP and port of the 'email' Service in otel-demo, and the checkout deployment configures EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080.

checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs logged repeated 'failed to send order confirmation to <user>: failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; the earliest matching line observed is 2026-11-15T12:27:53.627Z and the errors continue at least through 12:35:11Z.

The email Service has two Ready endpoint addresses on port 8080: 100.96.2.7 (email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn, node i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) and 100.96.3.218 (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, node i-071e7666000f6d243, the same node as checkout).

Both email pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState, containers started 2026-11-15T11:54:16Z, pods created 11:54:14Z and owned by ReplicaSet email-59f69bc6cf; all 22 otel-demo pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts.
The email deployment defines no readinessProbe, so a pod shows Ready as soon as its container runs; its only container port is 8080 (name 'service') and the Service targetPort is 8080.

email's own spans show normal handling of the requests that do arrive: operation 'POST /send_order_confirmation' recorded http.status_code=200 with durations of 4,576-64,179 us, and 'sinatra.render_template' 251-411 us, in the 12:31-12:33Z sample.

email's received-request rate for 'POST /send_order_confirmation' fell by roughly half across the incident onset: the two pod instances combined read 0.87-1.10 requests/s at 12:23-12:28Z but only 0.40-0.48 requests/s at 12:30-12:37Z, and both exported_instance series show nonzero activity during the incident.

Email pod memory working set stayed flat at about 51.2-51.9 MB against a 100Mi limit (checkout about 12.5-13.5 MB against 512Mi) over 12:12:32-12:37:32Z, so there is no memory-growth signature on email.

All five nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and NetworkUnavailable=False (reason CiliumIsUp); the only events in the window for email/checkout/frontend pods are Normal 'Updated' entries (no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy, Failed or restart events).

The frontend-proxy 504s are an upstream-timeout symptom of checkout's PlaceOrder blocking about 30s on email connection attempts, which exceeds the proxy's ~15.0s ingress timeout. The frontend->checkout parent-child edge is inferred, not observed: in the sampled trace the checkout spans' parent span id was not present in the returned view and the checkout client span's parent is the PlaceOrder span whose own parent was not shown.

TCP connection establishment to the email Service ClusterIP (100.67.49.77:8080) is failing for a large share of new connections (SYN unanswered, reported as 'i/o timeout') while the email application itself is healthy for connections it accepts; the mechanism could be dataplane/kube-proxy/conntrack behaviour, a dropped packet path, or a full listen/accept path, none of which the available evidence distinguishes.

A remaining candidate is that one of the two email endpoints is intermittently unreachable (which would explain a partial rather than total failure); counter-evidence is that both pod instances show request activity during the incident and both are Ready with valid endpoints, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded with the available per-endpoint reachability data.

Email pod crash, OOM kill or restart is ruled out as the cause: both email containers have restartCount 0 with empty lastState, pods were created 11:54:14Z before the incident, memory working set is flat near 51MB of a 100Mi limit, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/Unhealthy/Failed events exist in the window.

Email application error or slowness is ruled out as the failing step: email spans that were served returned http.status_code=200 in 4.6-64.2 ms with no ERROR status, and email's own error-rate series show only STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans.

A frontend-proxy-local fault is ruled out as the origin of the 504s: only its 'ingress' server spans error (all http.status_code 504 at ~15.0s), while its own 'router frontend egress' client spans have an error rate of 0 throughout the window, which matches an upstream request that exceeded the proxy timeout rather than a proxy-side failure.

Other checkout dependencies that were observed in the same traces completed normally with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 or no error status: e.g. cart POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 493 us, product-catalog GetProduct 92-345 us, currency Currency/Convert 770-941 us with otel.status_code=OK, shipping /get-quote 51,416 us, payment grpc charge 662 us, and checkout's own client spans to PaymentService/Charge, CartService/EmptyCart, CurrencyService/Convert and ProductCatalogService/GetProduct all recorded rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

Collect Cilium/Hubble flow and drop data and node TCP counters (conntrack usage, ListenDrops/ListenOverflows) for pod IPs 100.96.2.7:8080 and 100.96.3.218:8080 between 12:25Z and 12:40Z to identify why new connections to the email ClusterIP are silently dropped.

Add a readiness probe to the email deployment (none is defined today) so a container that is running but not accepting connections is removed from the email Service endpoints, and enable email request/accept logging to make that state observable.

gaps: Why new TCP connections to the email Service ClusterIP time out is not established: no packet capture, conntrack, Cilium/CNI policy or per-endpoint reachability data is available, and CiliumNetworkPolicy CRDs are not among the queryable kinds (the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no items and was not citable).
The email container produced no log lines at all in 11:27-12:46Z (both email pods returned no data), so accept-queue, listener and connection-error evidence from inside email is unavailable.

The alert rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by the Prometheus rule listing (no_data), so the rule's exact expression, window and the reported 0.2444444444444444 ratio could not be verified; the earliest clearly elevated 5-minute span error-rate sample is 12:30:32Z whereas the alert started at 12:27:32Z (the first logged email dial failure is 12:27:53Z, implying first failing dials around 12:27:23Z).

http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count returned no series for this target, so request-level HTTP status ratios and gRPC status-code error rates are unknown rather than zero.
No CPU throttling metric (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total) is available, so CPU starvation of the email containers cannot be assessed.
The change history integration is not available, so it cannot be checked whether any change to the email Service, its deployment or network configuration preceded 12:27Z.

Kubernetes objects reflect the cluster state at query time (about 12:46-12:49Z), not the state during 12:27-12:40Z; pod restartCount 0 and creation timestamps are cumulative but the objects cannot prove incident-time conditions.

Sampled trace views were partial: checkout spans in the trace analysed had parent span IDs that were not present in the returned view, so the frontend->checkout request edge is inferred rather than observed, and no complete call chain is claimed.
next_steps: Inspect Cilium/Hubble flows and drops plus node-level TCP listen-drop and conntrack counters for the two email pod IPs during 12:25-12:40Z.
Review the email service's application logs and enable request logging to check listen/accept behaviour during the window.
Retrieve and review the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition to confirm which metric and ratio produced the 0.2444 reading.
Add a readiness probe to the email deployment and consider retry/timeout tuning for checkout's email POST and the frontend-proxy 15s route timeout.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
